samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-10-29 to 2024-01-14. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A retrospective analysis, published on September 28, 2023, examined the key takeaways from New York Fashion Week (NYFW) for the Spring/Summer 2024 collections, which took place from September 8 to September 13, 2023. The event highlighted several major themes, including a fresh approach to brand presentation through innovative partnerships and experiences. A strong emphasis on diversity and inclusivity was evident on the runways; for instance, the brand Selkie featured models of all sizes, diverse skin tones, ages, gender identities, and included a wheelchair user. Similarly, Christian Siriano was praised for showcasing several plus-sized models of color. The analysis also pointed to a growing focus on sustainability within the industry, with designers like Ralph Lauren incorporating eco-conscious materials into their collections to demonstrate that style and sustainability can coexist. <2> New York Bridal Fashion Week, showcasing the Fall 2023 collections, took place from October 10-12, 2023. The official schedule was announced on September 25, 2023. The event featured a hybrid model of in-person runway shows, presentations, and appointments at various New York City locations, alongside digital releases on the Runway360 platform. The week highlighted collections from both established CFDA members like Andrew Kwon, Badgley Mischka, Monique Lhuillier, and Naeem Khan, and returning brands such as Amsale, Berta, and Pnina Tornai for Kleinfeld. It also served as a platform for emerging designers, including Andrea Osei, Bronx & Banco, Elly Sofocli, and Sébastien Luke, who presented their latest work. <3> In celebration of Creative Director Stuart Vevers's tenth anniversary with the brand, Coach presented its Spring 2024 collection with a runway show at the New York Public Library on September 7, 2023. The event kicked off New York Fashion Week, showcasing a collection that continued Vevers's exploration of modern youthfulness through the lens of Coach's American heritage. The collection featured tailored silhouettes, distressed leather, slip dresses, and denim, emphasizing a 'love-worn' beauty over perfection. It also highlighted the Coach (Re)Loved program by incorporating repurposed and upcycled materials. The show's front row included celebrities such as Jennifer Lopez, Lil Nas X, Camila Mendes, and Dove Cameron. <4> New York Fashion Week's Spring/Summer 2024 season occurred from September 8th to September 13th, 2023. The event commenced with Peter Do's inaugural collection for Helmut Lang and concluded with a show by LUAR. The official schedule, released by the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA), featured presentations from over 71 designers. A significant highlight of the week was the return of Ralph Lauren to the NYFW runway for the first time since September 2019. <5> On July 25, 2023, the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) and IMG released the preliminary schedule for New York Fashion Week (NYFW) September 2023. [2, 4] The event, which took place from September 8 to September 13, 2023, was set to feature the Spring/Summer 2024 collections from over 71 confirmed designers. [2, 3, 4] A significant highlight of the announcement was the return of several major American designers to the NYFW runway, including Ralph Lauren, Jonathan Cohen, and 3.1 Phillip Lim. [4] The week officially kicked off with Peter Do's debut show for Helmut Lang and concluded with a show by Luar. [2, 4] <6> Miami Swim Week®, recognized as the world's largest swim and resort wear festival, held its 2023 edition with events spanning from June into July. The main series of events, 'Miami Swim Week® The Shows,' took place from July 3rd to July 10th, 2023, featuring over 100 designers and more than 50 public and industry events across various Miami locations. The runway shows, a central component, began on July 5th at the SLS South Beach Hotel, which also hosted the VIP 'Splash Lounge' experience. The week strongly emphasized inclusivity and sustainability, notably hosting the first adaptive fashion show for individuals with disabilities and an eco-friendly trade show called Hammock. The Planet Fashion production company, however, held its collection of shows earlier, from June 8-11, 2023, at Hyde Beach at the SLS Hotel, as part of a coordinated effort with Paraiso to shift some events to June. The overall festival included numerous runway presentations, after-parties, and trade events like the Hammock Trade Show, which connected brands with buyers from July 8th to 10th. <7> A new version of the Fashion Sustainability and Social Accountability Act (the Fashion Act), designated as S.4746 in the Senate and A.4333 in the Assembly, was reintroduced in the New York State Legislature on February 14, 2023. [3, 7, 8] The bill targets fashion retailers and manufacturers that do business in New York and have a global revenue exceeding $100 million. [6, 9] The legislation aims to enhance transparency and hold these companies accountable for their social and environmental impacts. [6] If enacted, the act would compel these businesses to map their supply chains, perform comprehensive due diligence to identify and mitigate adverse impacts on human rights and the environment, and disclose these findings publicly. [6, 11] Furthermore, it mandates the establishment and achievement of science-based targets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, aligning with the objectives of the Paris Agreement. [6, 11] This reintroduction followed a 2022 version of the act that did not pass. [6, 9] <8> Designer Emma Gage's brand, Melke, made its New York Fashion Week runway debut with the Fall/Winter 2023 collection titled 'Peaches and Pests' on February 13, 2023. [1, 4] The collection, presented at Spring Studios, drew inspiration from Roald Dahl's classic book 'James and the Giant Peach' and Tim Burton's 1996 film adaptation. [1, 5] The line featured playful prints and quirky elements, such as a skirt with six attached arms, alongside bizarre silhouettes. [3] Showcasing a commitment to sustainability and global collaboration, the collection incorporated handcrafted peaches from Brooklyn, embroidered bugs from a Ukrainian artisan, and environmentally friendly, cruelty-free Italian wool and silk. [1, 6, 10] The show was noted as a significant debut for an emerging designer during the fashion week. [3, 6] <9> During New York Fashion Week, luxury lifestyle brand ELYSIAN hosted its inaugural 'CatWalk FurBaby' runway show on February 10, 2023, at Sony Hall to benefit animal welfare organizations. The cruelty-free fashion event paired ten designers with ten animal charities, competing for prize money. Designers included Malan Breton, Nicole Miller, and Marc Bouwer. Models walked the runway accompanied by rescue dogs. Vegan designer Marc Bouwer, a recipient of PETA's Humanitarian Award, walked with his model, a Yorkie, and a sign stating, "Adopt Don't Shop". A panel of celebrity judges, including fashion industry creator Fern Mallis and supermodel Carol Alt, awarded the first-place prize of $50,000 to the New York-based organization Global Strays. The event was hosted by Consuelo Vanderbilt Costin. <10> Thom Browne, who was announced as the new chairman of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) on October 11, 2022, with his term officially beginning January 1, 2023, made his notable return to the New York Fashion Week schedule after having shown in Paris for the previous two years. [3, 5] The announcement of his return was part of the preliminary NYFW schedule released on January 12, 2023. [8] His Fall/Winter 2023 runway show occurred as stated on Valentine's Day, February 14, 2023. [5, 9] The collection, which drew inspiration from Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's novella 'The Little Prince,' was presented at The Shed in Hudson Yards. [5, 10]

The lineup also included returning brands like Amsale, Berta, Markarian, Morilee Madeline Gardner, and Romona Keveza, along with the bridal debut of 2023 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist Tanner Fletcher. <3> The nonprofit IMPACT NYFW held its annual runway show during New York Fashion Week, showcasing nine emerging designers with a focus on sustainability and environmental advocacy. The event featured creative approaches to sustainable fashion, including multifunctional and reversible garments, zero-waste patterns, and the use of upcycled materials such as donated second-hand items, damaged goods, and scrap metals. The collection drew inspiration from Eastern elements, particularly the blossoming peony, which was artistically rendered on garments to symbolize a vibrant statement of Chinese originality on a Western stage. The show featured a blend of rich jewel tones, dainty pastels, flowing silhouettes, and intricate craftsmanship. Notably, the event took place during Lunar New Year celebrations and model Maye Musk closed the runway show, adding to its significance. The brand's goal was to bridge cultural divides by creating a new aesthetic that fuses Eastern femininity with Western style for the modern, powerful woman. <5> National Geographic made its New York Fashion Week debut on February 10, 2024, with "Fit for a Queen," an immersive runway show at Moonlight Studios in New York City. [2, 4, 8] The event, announced on January 31, 2024, was held to celebrate the upcoming premiere of the docu-series 'Queens,' which focuses on female-led animal societies. [3] The show was produced by the women-led agency Pop'N Creative and styled by Sakinah Bashir, featuring looks inspired by the animal kingdom. [2, 4] It blended fashion with technology, using holographic projections of animals like lions and elephants alongside models on the catwalk to create a 4D experience. [2, 4, 6] The show highlighted a diverse group of designers, including JêBlanc, Theophilio, Studio 189, Sergio Hudson, Bohn Jsell, anOnlyChild, Head of State, Bed on Water, Almasika, and L’Enchanteur, with footwear by Téjahn Burnet. [2, 4, 5] <6> IMG launched its first-ever consumer-focused pop-up, 'NYFW: Backstage,' from February 9-13, 2024, at 21 Greene Street in SoHo. [1, 5] This immersive event was created to provide the public with behind-the-scenes access to New York Fashion Week. [5] The experience, designed in consultation with creative director Ethan Tobman, featured a variety of interactive activations. [1, 7] Attendees had access to Q&A sessions with designers like Phillip Lim, Eckhaus Latta, Jason Wu, and Sergio Hudson. [1, 5] Other offerings included live-streamed runway shows, a TRESemmé Style Studio providing complimentary hair services, and an IMG Models Photo Studio where aspiring models could be photographed for a chance to be scouted. [2, 8] The pop-up also featured 'The Art of a Look' installation showcasing past designer creations, a Bluestone Lane Café, daily DJ sets, and the first-ever official NYFW merchandise capsule collection. [1, 2, 5] <7> During the Fall/Winter 2024 fashion season, significant controversies arose regarding the lack of size diversity and incidents of cultural appropriation, fueling ongoing demands for greater inclusivity and respect within the industry. A notable drop in plus-size model representation on the runways led to criticism that fashion's brief move towards body diversity was over. Concurrently, accusations of cultural appropriation gained prominence, exemplified by a dispute where Senegalese luxury brand Tongoro accused Balmain of plagiarizing its 'Cairo' face piece for their Fall/Winter Men's collection. This specific incident, which was highlighted following Paris Fashion Week Men's, sparked a broader conversation about the need for respectful engagement with cultural inspirations and equitable recognition for non-Western designers. <8> On January 13, 2024, it was announced that Derek Lam was appointed the new creative director for Câllas Milano. The brand was founded in 2020 by Lam's husband, Jan-Hendrik Schlottmann, and Marco Panzeri, and is inspired by Milanese style. Lam presented his first capsule collection for the brand on Saturday, February 10, 2024, which also marked the label's New York Fashion Week debut. <9> French designer Ludovic de Saint Sernin presented his Fall/Winter 2024 collection at New York Fashion Week (NYFW) on February 11, 2024, marking his first-ever runway show held outside of Paris. [4, 6, 8] The Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) officially announced the preliminary schedule, including de Saint Sernin's debut, on January 10, 2024. [3, 8] The collection, a collaboration with the Robert Mapplethorpe Foundation, drew inspiration from the late photographer's work, exploring themes of eroticism and the interplay between innocence and darkness. [5, 6, 7] This was a significant event for the brand, as North America is its largest market, accounting for 32% of total sales revenue. [2, 5] The show was a one-time event in New York, with the brand planning to return to the Paris Fashion Week schedule. [2] <10> The Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) announced the preliminary schedule for New York Fashion Week (NYFW) Fall/Winter 2024, which took place from February 9 to February 14, 2024. The official schedule featured over 70 confirmed designers, with Helmut Lang opening the week and Thom Browne closing the event. The lineup included returning brands such as Carolina Herrera, Coach, and Michael Kors, alongside the return of Monse, Lafayette 148, and Delpozo. Additionally, the schedule featured first-time appearances from designers like Bishme Cromartie and Jane Wade, and a much-anticipated New York debut for Ludovic de Saint Sernin.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Art Hearts Fashion hosted its 11th annual series of runway shows as part of Miami Swim Week from May 29 to June 2, 2024. The events commenced with a kick-off party on Wednesday, May 29, at The Gabriel South Beach, followed by runway shows from May 30 to June 2 at M2 in Miami Beach. The showcase featured a diverse and inclusive lineup of designers, with models of all shapes and sizes presenting the collections. Notable swimwear designers included Lila Nikole, BFYNE, Ca Rio Ca, Aussie Bum, Giannina Azar, Mister Triple X, and The Black Tape Project. The runway trends highlighted metallics, intricate embellishments, vibrant colors, and floral prints. <2> PARAISO Miami Beach, widely known as Miami Swim Week, held its 20th-anniversary event from May 30th to June 2nd, 2024. [3, 6] The four-day showcase of swimwear and resort wear took place at a state-of-the-art tent in Collins Park, Miami Beach, with additional events at various locations including the Miami Design District and W South Beach. [4, 5] The event, which unveiled the Resort 2025 collections, featured runway shows from a wide array of established and emerging designers such as ACACIA, Andrea Iyamah, Luli Fama, and Nike Swim. [2, 4] In addition to the fashion shows, the week included the 5th annual Istituto Marangoni Upcycle Challenge to promote sustainability in fashion, and a Summer Fashion Summit for industry leaders. [3, 4] The event drew over 30,000 attendees and 7,500 global buyers, highlighting its significant role in the global swimwear industry. [5, 6] <3> NYFW: Bridal, a key event in the bridal fashion calendar, took place in New York City from April 2 to April 4, 2024. [4, 1] Esteemed designers such as Reem Acra and Andrew Kwon held live shows, while Naeem Khan opted for intimate appointments. [4] The schedule also featured returning brands like Amsale, Berta, Markarian, and Morilee Madeline Gardner. [4] A notable highlight was the bridal debut of Tanner Fletcher, a 2023 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist. [4] <4> The Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) announced the official schedule for New York Fashion Week: Bridal, which occurred from April 2nd to April 4th, 2024. The lineup also included returning brands like Amsale, Berta, Markarian, Morilee Madeline Gardner, and Romona Keveza, along with the bridal debut of 2023 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist Tanner Fletcher. <5> The nonprofit IMPACT NYFW held its annual runway show during New York Fashion Week, showcasing nine emerging designers with a focus on sustainability and environmental advocacy. [5] The experience, designed in consultation with creative director Ethan Tobman, featured a variety of interactive activations. [1, 7] Attendees had access to Q&A sessions with designers like Phillip Lim, Eckhaus Latta, Jason Wu, and Sergio Hudson. [1, 5] Other offerings included live-streamed runway shows, a TRESemmé Style Studio providing complimentary hair services, and an IMG Models Photo Studio where aspiring models could be photographed for a chance to be scouted. [2, 8] The pop-up also featured 'The Art of a Look' installation showcasing past designer creations, a Bluestone Lane Café, daily DJ sets, and the first-ever official NYFW merchandise capsule collection. Concurrently, accusations of cultural appropriation gained prominence, exemplified by a dispute where Senegalese luxury brand Tongoro accused Balmain of plagiarizing its 'Cairo' face piece for their Fall/Winter Men's collection. This specific incident, which was highlighted following Paris Fashion Week Men's, sparked a broader conversation about the need for respectful engagement with cultural inspirations and equitable recognition for non-Western designers.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Philadelphia Fashion Week will celebrate its 20th anniversary with a six-day event from September 16-21, 2025, held at the historic former Strawbridge's department store building at 801 Market Street. The celebration, part of a yearlong series of events, will feature 51 designers, runway shows, industry panels, a style gala, and special shopping activations. Special guests confirmed to attend include Fern Mallis, the creator of New York Fashion Week, and Corey Smith, the head of diversity and inclusion at LVMH. A new feature for the anniversary is the debut of the Philadelphia Fashion Awards, designed to honor designers and creatives who are shaping the industry. The festivities will also include an Avant-Garde Ball and a Business of Fashion Panel. <2> A report on fashion supply chain risks and trends for 2025, published on February 6, 2025, draws its conclusions from the BoF-McKinsey State of Fashion Executive Survey, which polled 345 industry leaders between August and October 2024. The primary concerns identified for the year include the potential for new tariffs, particularly with a possible second term for Donald Trump, which could significantly impact sourcing costs. Another major risk is the continued robust enforcement of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA), pushing the industry towards greater supply chain transparency and stronger compliance frameworks. Additionally, a tight U.S. labor market is expected to create labor shortages and disruptions in warehouses and distribution centers. In response to these pressures, fashion brands are actively pursuing a multi-pronged strategy of diversifying their sourcing within Asia—strengthening partnerships in Vietnam, Bangladesh, and India—while also increasing investment in nearshoring to establish manufacturing hubs closer to key markets in Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean. <3> The Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) released the preliminary schedule for New York Fashion Week (NYFW) Fall/Winter 2025 on January 14, 2025. [5, 7] The event is scheduled to take place from Thursday, February 6, to Tuesday, February 11, 2025. [2, 3, 9] The calendar features over 52 runway shows and designer presentations. [2, 4, 5] As announced, Brandon Maxwell will open the week's events, and CFDA Chairman Thom Browne will close the week. [2, 4] This season marks the return of several notable designers to the NYFW schedule, including Altuzarra, Christopher John Rogers, and Calvin Klein Collection under the new creative direction of Veronica Leoni. [2, 4, 10] <4> In May 2025, Santa Fe will host two significant, concurrent Indigenous fashion events. The second annual SWAIA Native Fashion Week (SNFW), presented by the Southwestern Association for Indian Arts in collaboration with Vancouver Indigenous Fashion Week, will take place from May 7-11, 2025, featuring over 25 designers. [4, 10] Simultaneously, Native Fashion Week Santa Fe (NFWSF), founded by Amber-Dawn Bear Robe, will run from May 8-11, 2025. [8, 11] NFWSF is promoted as the largest collaborative showcase of Indigenous designers in North America, featuring over 30 designers and more than 100 models. [8] The event is dedicated to celebrating the blend of ancestral techniques with contemporary design, with a focus on sustainable, land-centered fashion and Indigenous couture. [3, 8] Both events aim to elevate Indigenous voices and establish Santa Fe as a major capital for Indigenous fashion. [7, 8] <5> The Miami Fashion Week® (MIAFW) November 2024 edition took place from November 19-23, 2024, across various locations in Miami. A retrospective report published on November 26, 2024, detailed the event's conclusion, which featured presentations from designers such as Philipp Plein, Lafayette 148 NY, and Giannina Azar. The week kicked off with a press conference at the Gary Nader Art Centre and a showcase by German designer Philipp Plein. Lafayette 148 NY held an outdoor runway show at Mr. C Miami Coconut Grove, while Giannina Azar presented her eveningwear collection at the Gary Nader Art Centre, featuring models who were also international pageant winners. The event also included an 'Influencers Brunch' where designer Shantall Lacayo unveiled her latest collection, and a two-day summit at Miami Dade College focused on sustainability and the future of fashion. The week's events were seen as reinforcing Miami's status as a cultural hub for global fashion. <6> A renewed and more integrated approach to technology is anticipated for the Fall 2025 fashion season, marking a shift from experimentation to widespread operational adoption of AI. Following a period of hype around technologies like NFTs, the industry is now focusing on practical applications that are reshaping design, supply chains, and consumer experiences. AI is being utilized as a creative partner in design, helping to generate patterns and assisting with material selection through advanced fabric simulation. In operations, AI is driving efficiency by enabling more accurate demand forecasting to reduce waste and optimize inventory. For consumers, the integration of AI aims to create hyper-personalized shopping experiences through tailored style recommendations, virtual try-ons, and customized content. This move towards embedding AI into core e-commerce platforms and operational back-ends signifies a deeper, more strategic implementation of technology within the fashion industry. <7> Miami Fashion Week (MIAFW), considered the second largest fashion event in the U.S., has scheduled its November 2024 edition to take place from November 19-23, 2024. [4] The event, which brings together designers, industry professionals, and fashion enthusiasts, will feature an expanded program of runway shows, exclusive activations, and sustainability-focused programming. [5, 6] Building on a successful January 2024 showcase that focused on streetwear, the November edition will broaden its traditional Resort wear legacy to include a wider variety of design genres. [5, 6] The lineup includes returning designers such as Ágatha Ruiz de la Prada, Yas González, and Giannina Azar, as well as new international brands like Claro Couture. [3, 8] A key feature is the new 'MiamiMade' initiative to support local designers. [6] In collaboration with Miami Dade College, MIAFW will also host an expanded two-day summit to discuss sustainability, the role of influencers, and the future of fashion. [5, 8] <8> The Festival of Arts Fine Art Show in Laguna Beach is scheduled to run from July 2 to August 29, 2025. A highlight of the season is the 16th annual 'Festival Runway Fashion Show,' which will take place on Sunday, August 10, 2025. During this event, exhibiting festival artists will showcase their creativity by designing and constructing unique couture garments made entirely from recycled, reclaimed, and repurposed materials. <9> Miami Fashion Week (MIAFW) held its November 2024 edition from November 19-23, featuring a blend of runway shows, exclusive activations, and sustainability-focused programming. [2, 5, 7] The designer lineup included headliner Lafayette 148 New York, which presented its Resort collection, alongside returning designers such as Ágatha Ruiz de la Prada, Giannina Azar, and Shantall Lacayo. [2, 6] The event also featured internationally renowned designer Philipp Plein and introduced the 'MiamiMade' initiative to support local talent like Sigal. [2, 6] Other featured designers included Yas González, Claro Couture, and Yenny Bastida. [6] A key component was the expanded two-day Miami Fashion Week Summit, held in collaboration with Miami Dade College, which focused on sustainable practices and the future of fashion. [5, 9] Activations included an exclusive book presentation by Ágatha Ruiz de la Prada and in-store events hosted by retailers. [8] <10> Produced by SFWRUNWAY, founded by Naomi Alabi, a NYFW Curve runway show took place on September 11, 2024, at The Ivy in Brooklyn, as part of New York Fashion Week. [1] The event, which focused on promoting inclusivity and body positivity, featured over 40 plus-size models showcasing collections from designers like West McCoy and Atiya Joanne Custom Couture. [1] This was the second NYFW Curve show of the year, following a launch event on February 9, 2024, which was also produced by SFWRUNWAY and billed as a groundbreaking plus-size runway show. [2, 3] The September show highlighted streetwear and couture, aiming to redefine fashion standards by celebrating the uniqueness of every body type. [1, 5]

For consumers, the integration of AI aims to create hyper-personalized shopping experiences through tailored style recommendations, virtual try-ons, and customized content. A highlight of the season is the 16th annual 'Festival Runway Fashion Show,' which will take place on Sunday, August 10, 2025. During this event, exhibiting festival artists will showcase their creativity by designing and constructing unique couture garments made entirely from recycled, reclaimed, and repurposed materials.
